label: Input KML folder
help: Folder of ADS-B KML tracks to process (one file per tail/day).

label: Airports CSV
help: The small per-airline airports file (header: airport,latitude,longitude,elevation_ft) produced by build_cirium_inputs.py. NOT the OurAirports Airports_*.txt database, and NOT the raw Cirium export.

label: Routes-time CSV
help: The per-airline route-time file (header: origin,destination,avg_enroute_min) produced by build_cirium_inputs.py. NOT the raw Cirium schedule export.

label: Output folder
help: Folder the output KML is written to.

label: Output filename
help: Name of the KML file to write; the GeoPackage gets the same name with .gpkg (a name ending in .gpkg names the GeoPackage itself). {from} and {to} are replaced by the first and last flight dates. A name is suggested from the input batch and enabled features.

label: Output format
help: both writes <name>.gpkg (GeoPackage for QGIS and direct_detect) next to <name>.kml (Google Earth); gpkg writes only the GeoPackage (fastest); kml writes only the KML.
example: both keeps the KML you have today and adds the GeoPackage beside it.

label: Airline code
help: Airline recorded in the GeoPackage (flights.airline and the meta table).

label: GeoPackage track points
help: Also write the per-point track_points layer (time, altitude, ground speed, vertical speed, track and source per point); about 10x the size of the flights layer. Always on when positions are integrated.
example: on for altitude/speed colouring and the time slider in QGIS.

label: QGIS project (.qgz)
help: Also write <name>.qgz next to the GeoPackage: a QGIS project (built by ~/Git/qgis prepare) linking it with the navdb chart layers, basemaps and styles. Needs Output format both or gpkg, and a navdb.
example: on, with the navdb below, to open the flights in the Route Explorer.

label: navdb GeoPackage
help: navdb_<AIRAC>.gpkg for the QGIS project's chart layers (airways, fixes, FIRs, procedures). Linked, not copied. Required for the QGIS project.

label: Company routes GeoPackage
help: Optional company_routes GeoPackage from company_route_extractor. With it the QGIS project matches flights to company routes; without it, flown routes only.

label: Sample interval (min)
help: Point sampling interval in minutes; larger = smaller files, coarser lines.

label: Max in-flight gap (min)
help: A time gap larger than this splits one flight segment into two.
example: 20 tolerates a 20-minute ADS-B dropout within a flight.

label: Group by
help: Organize the output KML folders by origin or destination airport.
example: destination groups all arrivals into an airport together.

label: Confidence preset
help: Detection/recovery aggressiveness. strict = proximity only; permissive = widest recovery for sparse coverage.
example: permissive for sparse Latin-America ADS-B; balanced for dense US/EU.

label: Airport match radius (km)
help: Override the preset's airport-proximity radius for endpoint detection.
example: 100 (permissive default) matches an airport within 100 km of a track end.

label: Max join gap (h)
help: Override max time gap for joining two fragments of one flight across files.
example: 4 lets fragments up to 4 hours apart join.

label: Max join distance (km)
help: Override max spatial gap (km) allowed when joining fragments.

label: Route-time tolerance
help: Override route-time match tolerance (fraction). Higher = looser, more recoveries.
example: 0.60 = accept enroute times within +/-60% of the scheduled average.

label: Corridor cross-track (km)
help: The main recovery/noise knob. Lower = stricter (less mis-attribution, fewer recoveries).
example: 50 with the permissive preset gives the recommended clean-and-complete result.

label: Route-time rescue
help: Force route-time rescue on or off, overriding the preset. Blank = use preset.
example: on forces rescue even under the strict preset.

label: Color mode
help: source colors lines by data source (ADS-B/POS/firehose); altitude uses the ADS-B Exchange altitude gradient.
example: altitude paints climb->cruise->descent from orange through blue to magenta.

label: Line color
help: Override the line color (source mode only). KML AABBGGRR.

label: Line width
help: Override line width in pixels.

label: Opacity (%)
help: Line opacity 0-100 (100 = opaque).

label: Show labels
help: Show a per-flight name label on each track.
example: true labels each flight with its route.

label: Show airport icons
help: Draw an airport icon at endpoints.
example: true shows a marker at each airport.

label: Extrude to ground
help: Extrude the 3-D flight path down to the ground.
example: true draws vertical drop-lines under the track.

label: Altitude bands
help: Number of discrete color steps in altitude mode (more = smoother, bigger file).
example: 24 gives ~1700 ft per band over 0-40000 ft.

label: Stitch coverage gaps
help: Draw straight-line connectors across coverage gaps in a distinct color to mark inferred data.
example: true splits a flight into real placemarks + gray connectors.

label: Inferred color
help: KML AABBGGRR color for inferred gap connectors.

label: Stitch gap threshold (min)
help: Minutes between points above which a gap connector is drawn.

label: Integrate position sources
help: Fill in-flight ADS-B gaps with real ACARS POS and/or firehose fixes (detection unchanged).
example: true requires the POS/firehose folders + tail-icao below.

label: ACARS POS folder
help: Folder of ACARS position-report JSON files (keyed to hex via the mapping CSV).

label: ADS-B firehose folder
help: Folder of ADS-B firehose position JSON files (carry ICAO hex directly).

label: Tail<->ICAO CSV
help: CSV mapping tail_number,icao_hex — required to key ACARS POS to hex.

label: POS color
help: KML AABBGGRR color for ACARS-POS-sourced portions.

label: Firehose color
help: KML AABBGGRR color for firehose-sourced portions.
